answer: The defence rests on hurling club tenure with championship appearance history: championships played under one club for years. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The ivory signal separates the two cases at a glance: Forging 566 of these means building 566 separate appearance histories from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The river ledger records each payment, the ocean window resets the board, and 566 fakes never beat one honest agent on price.
